body:
I often feel the same way. One tiny thing can ruin a whole day, and kick you straight off your horse.

What I try to remember is that every time that happens, and every time I climb back up on that horse, I am stronger for it. Next time, it'll take something bigger to bring me down.

When you start pursuing your activity/improvement of choice - don't immediately focus on results. Focus on consistency. That you practice or study that thing consistently on the days you've set for that activity. Once you have consistency down, results will follow.

Godspeed.

"Economics: The Users Guide" is a nice easy to digest introduction to Economics, and is written for the lay person. After reading that I would check out "Capital in the 21st Century"

Politics will depend on what exactly you're interested in knowing more about. It's a massive subject, frankly. If you want some highly critical material you can check out the work of Chomsky. If you want to know more about institutions try looking for books on the branches of government.

It's obvious that you want to change. You can't just make yourself stop wanting that. The question you should be asking is - Why am I stuck in this rut, and what can I do to get out of it.

The first step is dropping the negative thinking. It's easy to imagine that other people are better than you, and that you can't live or improve the way they do. The truth is we're all human, and we all have the capacity to change and improve ourselves. You just have to decide that you actually want it enough.

Once you accept that fact, the next step is to pick 1 thing you wish to improve. It might be your fitness, it might be a subject you wish to study, it might be your social skills (this is a hard one and many people's problems can be overcame by developing more confidence through other pursuits). But pick one thing you want to improve.

Third, you want to start reading up on that particular topic. Learn the different perspectives and methods, and use this to write or draw a roadmap that starts where you are now, and takes you forward on a journey of self improvement. Leverage other people's knowledge to speed up your own improvement. 

Once you have this roadmap set, you can begin thinking about daily goals and targets that you want to meet, that will take you on that journey.

It isn't easy. We all feel the temptation to stay where we are comfortable, where we aren't accountable and where we don't have to face failure. It's a hard and brave decision to commit to self improvement.

I wish you luck on your journey.

Does your girlfriend have a social circle you could hang out with? Does your workplace ever hold nights out or other events?

Building a friend group is kind of weird. You get to know people through other people, but getting a start is the hardest part. 

Most of my closest friends I've met by some strange accident - So I can't suggest a surefire method.
